hadith:
Witr Prayer - Narrated Sa`id bin Yasar:

I was going to Mecca in the company of `Abdullah bin `Umar and when I apprehended the approaching dawn, I dismounted and offered the witr prayer and then joined him. `Abdullah bin `Umar said, "Where have you been?" I replied, "I apprehended the approaching dawn so I dismounted and prayed the witr prayer." `Abdullah said, "Isn't it sufficient for you to follow the good example of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)?" I replied, "Yes, by Allah." He said, "Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) used to pray witr on the back of the camel (while on a journey)."
message:
# Spiritual Reflection

Allah reminds us through His name Al-Khaafid (The Abaser) that all status and position come from Him alone, so we should not attach our hearts to worldly rank or seek validation from others. Just as the Prophet (ﷺ) remained devoted to prayer regardless of his circumstances—even while traveling—we too should maintain our spiritual priorities and trust in Allah's wisdom above all else. By keeping our focus on pleasing Allah rather than gaining the approval of others, we find true honor and peace in submission to Him.
name:
Al Khaafid - الْخَافِضُ - The Abaser

Al Khaafid emphasizes the power of Allah in altering circumstances and statuses, both by raising some and lowering others. The concept reflects His sovereignty and control over all creation, highlighting that one's worth or position is ultimately determined by Him.
verse:
Al-Ma'idah - The Table Spread - 5:51

O believers! Take neither Jews nor Christians as guardians—they are guardians of each other. Whoever does so will be counted as one of them. Surely Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
